findings.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 stores feed content as raw_html without sanitization; CGI.unescapeHTML can convert escaped script markup into executable HTML, causing persistent XSS.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 validates the URL host only before open-uri follows redirects, allowing redirects from an approved host to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (SSRF).

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:12 passes the full referrer URL to postMessage as targetOrigin instead of a URL origin, so referrers containing paths can raise SyntaxError and prevent iframe resizing.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 unconditionally calls scrub on i.content; RSS items containing only description cause NoMethodError and abort the polling run.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 calls downcase on a potentially blank SiteSetting.embed_by_username, causing every retrieval job to fail when an embeddable host is enabled without configuring the default-blank setting.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative, rewriting URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png incorrectly and corrupting imported links and images.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38 expects TopicRetriever#retrieve even though the controller enqueues a retrieve_topic job, so the test cannot satisfy its expectation or verify the asynchronous behavior.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 validates message origins using substring matching rather than exact origin equality and does not verify e.source, allowing forged resize messages from a distinct origin that prefixes the configured forum URL.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same security vulnerability as the golden comment. Both point out that the origin validation using substring/indexOf matching (rather than exact equality) is insufficient and can be bypassed by a malicious domain that prefixes or contains the configured forum URL. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 stores feed content as raw_html without sanitization; CGI.unescapeHTML can convert escaped script markup into executable HTML, causing persistent XSS.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 33, content is processed with CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) and passed to TopicEmbed.import(). In TopicEmbed.import(), the content is stored with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], which means in Post#cook (app/models/post.rb lines 131-133), it returns raw content directly without any sanitization: 'return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'. The content is then rendered in views using 'raw post.cooked' (app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 17). This creates a clear XSS vulnerability path: RSS feed content -> CGI.unescapeHTML (which can convert <script> to <script>) -> stored as raw_html -> rendered without sanitization. This is a real security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 validates the URL host only before open-uri follows redirects, allowing redirects from an approved host to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (SSRF).

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in lib/topic_retriever.rb the `invalid_host?` method checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` before fetching. Then in `fetch_http`, it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`. In lib/app/models/topic_embed.rb, `import_remote` uses `open(url).read` with ruby-readability. The validation happens before the HTTP request, but `open-uri` follows redirects automatically. An attacker could set up a page on the approved embeddable_host that redirects to an internal service (like cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254). The host validation only checks the initial URL, not the final destination after redirects. This is a legitimate SSRF vulnerability - the code validates the URL host before making the request, but open-uri will follow redirects to arbitrary destinations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 calls downcase on a potentially blank SiteSetting.embed_by_username, causing every retrieval job to fail when an embeddable host is enabled without configuring the default-blank setting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:50, the code is `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`. If `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is blank (empty string), calling `.downcase` on an empty string returns an empty string, which won't cause an error. However, if it's `nil`, calling `.downcase` on `nil` would raise a NoMethodError. Looking at config/site_settings.yml, `embed_by_username` is defined with default value `''` (empty string), not nil. So it would be an empty string, not nil, and `.downcase` on empty string works fine. The query would just return no user, and the method returns early with `return if user.blank?`. This is not a crash scenario - it's handled gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative, rewriting URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png incorrectly and corrupting imported links and images.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-68, the absolutize_urls method checks if href/src start_with?('/') and then prepends the prefix. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/image.png' do start with '/', so they would be incorrectly rewritten to something like 'http://eviltrout.com//cdn.example.com/image.png'. This is a real bug - the code should check for '//' prefix to exclude protocol-relative URLs, or use a more robust URL parsing approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38 expects TopicRetriever#retrieve even though the controller enqueues a retrieve_topic job, so the test cannot satisfy its expectation or verify the asynchronous behavior.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb line 14-15, when topic_id is nil, the controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` which is an asynchronous job. In the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38-42, the test sets up `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil)` and then expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. However, since the controller enqueues an async job rather than calling TopicRetriever directly, the TopicRetriever mock expectations would never be satisfied during the controller action itself. The actual TopicRetriever call happens in the job (lib/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), not in the controller. This is a real test bug - the test expectations don't match the actual code flow.
